title: D2-2b: Extremely Narrow Pressure Window under a Product-Flow Band
question_prompt:
D2-2b: Extremely Narrow Pressure Window under a Product-Flow Band

The SWRO train is healthy, but the downstream post-treatment unit can only accept a permeate-flow band of 6.900–6.910 m³/h. Feed flow is locked at 4.30 kg/s, so only Pressure may be adjusted. At 0.05-bar resolution, locate the Pressure window satisfying the product-flow band, Recovery, Flux, and water quality. A single PASS is not enough; both sides of the window must be demonstrated.

Feed | Temperature | 32 | °C; fixed | Qp maximum | None | No upper limit
Membrane | Effective membrane area | 400 | m²; fixed | Recovery maximum | 46 | %
Membrane | A_comp | 4.2e-12 | m/s/Pa; fixed | Flux maximum | 18 | LMH
Membrane | B_comp | 3.4e-08 | m/s; fixed | Salt rejection minimum | 98.7 | %

Hydraulics | Pressure drop | 0.653 | bar | Current setpoint | 52.90 bar / 4.30 kg/s | Permeate flow is above the downstream band
Channel | Channel height | 0.002 | m | Feed flow | Fixed at 4.30 kg/s | Not adjustable
Channel | Spacer porosity | 0.75 | - | Pressure candidates | 52.60 / 52.65 / 52.90 bar | Both sides of the window must be shown
Channel | Equivalent module length | 20 | m | Objective | Complete feasible window | Do not stop at the first PASS
Model | Concentration polarization / mass transfer | calculated | WaterTAP calculated

Required Tasks
1. Explain why 52.90 bar is unacceptable as the current setpoint.
2. Search downward and test whether 52.65 bar satisfies every constraint.
3. Test 52.60 bar to establish whether the lower boundary is Qp-controlled.
4. Combine the 52.90 upper-side failure with the 52.60 lower-side failure and report the complete feasible Pressure window at 0.05-bar resolution.

Task boundary: In D2-2b, feed conditions, membrane properties, area, and system structure remain fixed. The problem arises from the operating setpoint or the allowed operating envelope. Do not change feed quality, temperature, membrane area, or A/B.
